how-many.html.text:
← Porta potty event quote calculator

How many porta potties for 200 people?

Event planners type that question every weekend. Portable sanitation yards get it from the other side: a bride or a festival promoter wants a Saturday special, and the yard has to decide how many boxes to send and what to charge once those boxes sit Friday through Sunday.

This page is a planning starting point, not a health-code table, an ADA determination, or a recommendation of what any event must provide. Local rules and the actual layout of the site always win. Use the quote calculator to price the days, pump-outs, and miles once you have a fleet in mind.

A starting restroom count for 200 attendees

These figures use a common event-planning pattern: more people per restroom on a short event, fewer people per restroom as the day gets longer, and about 20% more restrooms when alcohol is served. They are not a published standard.

Event lengthNo alcoholAlcohol served
Up to 4 hours4 restrooms5 restrooms
5–6 hours5 restrooms7 restrooms
7–8 hours7 restrooms9 restrooms
9–10 hours8 restrooms10 restrooms
11–12 hours10 restrooms13 restrooms

Whenever restrooms go out, plan on at least one wheelchair-accessible unit (and more than one on a large public site). If food is served, add handwash stations — often about one per four restrooms as a starting split.

Why the Saturday special still loses money

Even if four or five units is the right count, pricing them as “200 people × a flat unit price” misses the lines that actually cost the yard:

  • Days on site. Friday drop through Sunday pickup is three days of rent, not one Saturday.
  • Two truck round trips. Delivery is a round trip. Pickup is a second round trip. Mileage is four times the one-way distance.
  • Pump-outs. A one-day drop-and-pickup often needs none. A box that sits overnight usually needs a service visit.

A $125 Saturday special on five units is $625. On a typical 18-mile two-day wedding with one pump-out, that number is often below cost before overhead.

Price the event in the calculator →

Questions people actually ask

How many porta potties for a 200-person wedding?

Start from the 4-hour or 8-hour row above, depending on how long guests stay, and add a wheelchair-accessible unit. Then price Friday–Sunday, not Saturday only.

How many porta potties for a festival or 5K?

Longer events and alcohol both raise the starting count. Peak arrival (a race finish, a concert gate) matters more than average headcount — the calculator does not model surge, so add units if the crowd hits the restrooms at once.

Do I need ADA porta potties?

Public events usually need accessible units. This tool does not decide that. It can include wheelchair-accessible units in a quote; whether they satisfy ADA or local rules is a question for the event and a qualified professional.

Common questions

How many porta potties for 200 people?

A common planning starting point is about 4 restrooms for a 4-hour event without alcohol, 7 for an 8-hour event, and about 9 if that 8-hour event also serves alcohol. Add at least one wheelchair-accessible unit. These are planning estimates, not a health-department or ADA determination.

Does a Saturday wedding only need one day of rental?

Usually no. Friday drop through Sunday pickup is three calendar days of rent, plus two truck round trips, even if the ceremony is only Saturday afternoon.

Do I need a pump-out for a one-day event?

A single-day drop-and-pickup often needs no extra service visit. Multi-day rentals usually need a pump-out for each extra day the boxes sit.

No warranty. This free page is not legal, tax, financial, engineering, or health-department advice. It does not determine how many units an event requires or whether a site is compliant. Verify against local rules and a qualified professional. To the maximum extent permitted by law, the authors accept no liability for loss or damage from its use.

FOR PORTABLE SANITATION YARDS

Bid the extra days and the pump-outs, not the Saturday headcount.

Price a porta potty / portable restroom event rental the way the yard actually loses money when it skips the math: every day the boxes sit, every extra pump-out, and two round trips of truck miles. You get the quote, the price per unit-day, and the number below which the job loses money. A starting fleet estimate from attendance is optional — it is not a health-code determination.

The event

Days on site includes drop day and pickup day. Friday drop through Sunday pickup is three days, not one Saturday. Attendance is optional and only used for a starting fleet estimate.

The fleet

One row per unit type. Daily rent is what the box earns sitting; service each is the pump-out price for that type. Starting rates are ballpark figures — replace them with your book.

Where the money goes

    Transparent arithmetic from your own inputs. The starting daily rents, pump-out prices, and fleet estimate are common ballpark figures, not a tariff, a health-code table, or a guarantee. Replace them with your book and confirm local requirements before sending a quote.

    Common questions

    Why is a Friday-drop, Sunday-pickup weekend billed as three rental days, not one?

    Because the unit sits on site and the yard's capital is tied up for every day between drop-off and pickup, not just the day of the event. A flat “Saturday special” that prices only the event day undercounts the rent by however many extra days the box actually occupies the lot.

    Does the suggested fleet size tell me how many units my event legally needs?

    No. The people-per-unit figures are a starting planning estimate by event length, not a health-department code table or a permit requirement — local ordinances and venue rules may require more (or specify accessible-unit ratios) than this tool suggests. Confirm with your local health authority before finalizing a fleet for a permitted event.

    Why does mileage get charged twice?

    Delivery is a round trip to drop units off, and pickup is a separate round trip to retrieve them — two trips, not one, even though it's the same event. If your yard also does a mid-event service run, that's an additional round trip the pump-out count should reflect.

    Does alcohol at the event actually change the numbers, or is that just a note?

    It's a real adjustment: checking it shortens the people-per-unit figure by 20%, which raises the suggested fleet size, because alcohol consumption is a common industry planning adjustment for restroom demand. It is not a health-code rule, just a starting assumption you can override.

vs-a-flat-saturday-special-price.html.text:
← Porta Potty Event Quote Calculator

This calculator vs. a flat Saturday-special price

“$150 a unit for Saturday” prices the event day. It does not see the Friday drop, the Sunday pickup, the extra pump-out, or the second round trip — the four lines that turn a job that looked like last week's into one that loses money.

What a flat Saturday-special price is

A flat Saturday-special price is a single per-unit dollar figure, quoted for the event day and multiplied by however many units the promoter says they need. It is fast to say on the phone, and it is the number a promoter holding one yard's quote will read back to the next yard and ask them to match.

The figure was set once, usually against a same-day drop-and-pickup job with no extra pump-out and a short haul, and then reused for every booking under the same headcount — whether the actual job is that same-day booking or a full weekend with the boxes sitting three days, an extra service visit, and a delivery yard forty miles out instead of five.

What this calculator is

This page keeps no account and sends nothing to a server. You enter your unit mix and their per-day rent and per-visit service price, the days the boxes actually sit on site, service (pump-out) visits, delivery and pickup fees, one-way mileage and your rate per mile, an optional weekend haul premium, consumables per unit, overhead, and target margin. It prices the rental days, the pump-outs, and the full two-round-trip haul as their own lines and returns the event price, the price per unit-day, and the walk-away price below which the job loses money — for this event's own days and trips, not a per-unit number set from a different booking.

What a flat Saturday-special price doesWhat this calculator does instead
Charges the same per-unit figure whether the boxes sit for the event day alone or for a full Friday-through-Sunday weekend. Prices rent per unit for every day on site, so a three-day sit costs three times what a one-day sit costs — on this booking, not the headcount average.
Has no separate line for an extra pump-out during a multi-day event. Prices service visits per unit, per visit, so an added pump-out is priced when it is booked, not absorbed into a flat number that never planned for it.
Prices one truck trip, when a delivery and a pickup are two — four times the one-way mileage, not one. Prices delivery, pickup, and mileage as a full round-trip haul, plus an optional weekend premium on that haul.
Gives the yard a number to quote against a promoter's ask, not a number to check that ask against. Reports the walk-away price and flags a proposed price that falls below break-even, so a shopped number can be scored before you agree to match it.
Has no view of the fleet a headcount actually needs. This calculator's own fleet-size estimate from attendance, event length, and alcohol/food service.

Same five units, one flat price

Using this calculator's own shipped fleet — four standard portable restrooms and one wheelchair-accessible unit, $85 delivery, $85 pickup, 18 miles one way at $3.50 a mile, $8 per unit in consumables, 12% overhead, and a 25% target margin:

A genuine weekend booking — Friday drop through Sunday pickup, three days on site, one extra mid-weekend pump-out — costs $1,061.76 to run before a dollar of profit, and this calculator prices it at $1,415.68.

A flat Saturday-special quote of $150 a unit for the same five units comes to $750: $311.76 below the job's own break-even cost — before counting the $665.68 it falls short of this calculator's own price at the same 25% target margin. Same five units, same weekend, one flat number that loses money the moment the extra day, the extra pump-out, and the second round trip are counted.

Common questions

Why does a flat Saturday-special price get an event rental wrong?

Because a flat per-unit Saturday price prices the event day, not the rental. A promoter shopping yards for "$150 a unit for Saturday" is asking every yard to quote the same number for a job that is not the same job everywhere: one yard drops Friday and picks up Monday, another drops and picks up same-day; one event needs an extra mid-weekend pump-out, another does not; one site is five miles from the yard, another is forty. The unit count is the only variable the flat price sees, and it is not the only variable the job has.

What does a flat Saturday-special price usually leave out entirely?

The days on site beyond the event itself, the pump-out visits, and one of the two round trips. Rent is normally charged for every day a unit sits -- Friday drop through Sunday pickup is three days, not one -- but a flat per-unit number is set once against a typical single-day job and then quoted for every booking. It has no separate line for an extra pump-out, and it prices one truck trip when a delivery and a pickup are two round trips: four times the one-way mileage, not one.

How big is the pricing gap in practice?

On this calculator's own shipped fleet -- four standard units and one wheelchair-accessible unit, $85 delivery, $85 pickup, 18 miles one way at $3.50/mile, $8/unit consumables, 12% overhead, 25% target margin -- a genuine Friday-through-Sunday weekend booking with one extra pump-out costs $1,061.76 to run and this calculator prices it at $1,415.68. A flat Saturday-special quote of $150 a unit for the same five units comes to $750: $311.76 below the job's own break-even cost, before counting the $665.68 it falls short of this calculator's own price at the same 25% target margin. Same five units, same weekend, one number that loses money the moment the extra day, the extra pump-out, and the second round trip are counted.

Is a flat Saturday-special price ever the right way to quote?

For a same-day drop-and-pickup job with no extra pump-out and a short haul -- the case the flat number was probably set from -- it can land close. The risk is the multi-day weekend booking under the identical per-unit ask, because the flat price does not know how many days the boxes will actually sit, how many pump-outs the site will need, or how far the yard is driving until the booking details are in, and by then the flat number has often already been quoted.

Does this calculator know my local rental or pump-out rates?

No. It has no price book and no data on your market's going rate. It takes your own per-unit rent and service price, the days the boxes actually sit, pump-out visits, delivery and pickup fees, mileage, and your target margin, and turns that into a price for this event -- the arithmetic a flat Saturday-special number skips, not a market survey.

vs-servicecore.html.text:
← Porta Potty Event Quote Calculator

This calculator vs. ServiceCore

Two different shapes: ServiceCore is an account-based platform for running a portable sanitation yard's whole fleet, routes, and billing. This page is a free, private worksheet for one question — what should this event rental cost, given its days, pump-outs, and fleet mix — before you send the quote.

What each tool is for

ServiceCore is business-management software, founded in 2017, built specifically for portable restroom, septic, and dumpster rental operators — a narrower niche than general field-service platforms, and the company states it hires more people out of the portable sanitation and dumpster industries than any other software company in that space. It bundles customer and asset (unit and truck) management, route planning and scheduling, and accounting tools including estimates, invoices, and payment processing into one ongoing account, aimed at operators running multiple trucks across a standing customer base rather than a single one-off rental. ServiceCore's own pricing page is not reachable from this session to confirm today's plan names or any dollar figure, so no price for it is invented here: only its well-documented identity and category — fleet- and route-management software for portable sanitation and rolloff operators, sold as an ongoing account — are stated, and no dollar amount for ServiceCore appears on this page.

This calculator does none of what ServiceCore does. It does not track a customer, route a truck, or bill recurring service, and it stores no customer or job record on a server. It takes one event — attendance, duration in days, a mix of standard, deluxe, ADA-accessible, and hand-wash units, pump-out visits, and the two round trips (delivery and pickup) a flat headcount rate hides — plus your rates, loaded labor, and target margin, and turns that into the event price, the price per unit-day, a starting fleet-size estimate from attendance and duration, and the walk-away price below which the job loses money — plus, if you already have a number on the table, a check of whether it clears that walk-away floor, and a single printable customer proposal for that one event. It runs free in any browser, keeps no account, and uploads nothing you type.

How much does a Friday-drop, Sunday-pickup weekend actually add over a single-day rate, beyond the extra units?This calculator's separate days-on-site, pump-out, and two-round-trip line items — a flat headcount special hides all three.
A customer's budget is below what I'd normally quote. Does it still clear my walk-away floor?This calculator's proposed-price check — it flags a price below break-even before you agree to it.
I need my whole fleet, routes, and recurring billing running from one shared account across the season.ServiceCore — built as an ongoing, account-based platform for exactly that job.
How many units does an event this size actually need?This calculator's own fleet-size estimate.
Do I need to create an account or sign up to use the tool?This calculator: no. ServiceCore is used through an ongoing account built for multi-truck operators, not a one-off event quote.

Most portable sanitation yards get different value from each: ServiceCore (or a comparable platform) for running the yard's whole fleet-to-invoice operation as an ongoing account, and a private calculator like this one for an instant, no-login answer to what one event rental should cost from its days, pump-outs, and fleet mix before a business system is involved. This page's own figures are a pricing model, not a customer record, a routed job, or a signed contract.

This tool needs no account and no sign-in: it is a static page, the arithmetic runs in your browser, and once it has loaded it keeps working with the connection off.

Common questions

Should I use this calculator or ServiceCore?

They do different jobs, and a portable sanitation yard of any size will likely end up touching both eventually. ServiceCore, founded in 2017, builds business-management software specifically for portable restroom, septic, and dumpster rental operators — the company says it hires more people out of the portable sanitation and dumpster industries than any other software company in that space. It bundles customer and asset management, route planning and scheduling, and accounting tools including estimates, invoices, and payment processing into one ongoing account, aimed at operators running multiple trucks across a standing customer base. ServiceCore's own pricing page is not reachable from this session to confirm today's plan names or any dollar figure, so no price for it is invented here: only its well-documented identity and category — fleet- and route-management software for portable sanitation and rolloff operators, sold as an ongoing account — are stated, and no dollar amount for ServiceCore appears on this page. This calculator does one narrower thing: starting from one event's attendance, duration, unit mix, pump-out visits, and the two round trips a flat headcount rate hides, plus your rates and target margin, it turns that into the event price, the price per unit-day, a starting fleet-size estimate, and the walk-away price below which the job loses money, plus a printable customer proposal for that one event — before any of it touches a route or billing system.
